newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus police arrest Greenpeace activists.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus police arrest Greenpeace activists.

text.p: Eight Greenpeace activists were arrested in Cyprus on Thursday when they blocked the entrance to a government building to urge authorities to protect the island's northwestern Akamas Peninsula.
Police said the detainees, three women and five men, will appear in court on Friday morning. The activists are from Greece, Malta, Italy, the Netherlands, Norway and the United States.
The activists had chained themselves to the gates of the ministry of agriculture and natural resources in capital Nicosia for 90 minutes.
"They are held on suspicion of causing a disturbance, trespassing and criminal intervention," a police spokesman told Reuters.
Police armed with clippers broke the chains off the demonstrators and hauled them into waiting police vans.
"We warned them to leave peacefully, they refused and we were forced to cut the chains off them and arrest them," deputy divisional police commander Michalakis Kouis said.

Greenpeace and local environment groups who took part in the protest have been urging the Cyprus authorities for years to turn the Akamas, an uninhabited peninsula and important turtle nesting area into a protected zone.
"We have been coming here for eight years, there have been promises but nothing concrete ever happened," said Mario Damato of the Greenpeace Mediterranean office.
Environmentalists fear that failure to protect Akamas could result in mass development which has marred other coastlines of the eastern Mediterranean island.
